newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Taleban capture north Afghan province of Kunduz.
newsitem.headline: Taleban capture north Afghan province of Kunduz.

text.p: The northern Afghan province of Kunduz, held by joint opposition forces, fell to the Taleban Islamic militia on Sunday, a Pakistan-based Afghan news service said.

The Afghan Islamic Press (AIP) quoted its sources in Afghanistan as saying that the entire province including its capital, also named Kunduz, was captured by the Taleban after light clashes with forces loyal to northern Uzbek leader General Abdul Rashid Dostum and ousted president Burhanuddin Rabbani.
AIP said three opposition soldiers were killed and more than 150 captured by the Taleban after a limited clash with forces of Ahmed Shah Masood, top military commander of Rabbani.
It said white Taleban flags were flying in the city.
The report of the fall of Kunduz came hours after Taleban warriors and their new-found Uzbek allies swept into the north Afghan city of Mazar-i-Sharif virtually unopposed.
Earlier on Saturday, the Taleban had captured the northern town of Shibarghan, Dostum's military headquarters and main airbase, hours after a mutiny in his small air force.
